public_factual_controls.pre_1950_context: Three Early Phrygian inscriptions G-101 to G-103 were known from the Korte excavations of 1900; one had been misidentified as Greek.
public_factual_controls.american_excavations: Excavations beginning in 1950 demonstrated major epigraphic richness.
public_factual_controls.published_summary: Public Digital Gordion states 11 inscriptions on stone and 245 graffiti, primarily on vases, and says Gordion remains the richest site for Early Phrygian epigraphy.
public_factual_controls.publication_lineage: Digital Gordion attributes publication of the inscriptions to C. Brixhe and M. Lejeune and cites Young 1969 as an earlier survey.

denominator_policy: 11 stone inscriptions and 245 graffiti are source-reported Gordion Early Phrygian category counts, not a project-certified unique-object total.
Do not merge these counts with TITUS headings, TM attestations, or UD identities without record-level reconciliation.
Use Digital Gordion as an institutional factual/discovery witness; it does not independently certify every reading.

new_frontier.reason: The monumental web lane omits most small objects, while the institutional Gordion source establishes a much larger published graffiti population.
